references.text: The sons of Merari were responsible for the planks, bars, pillars, bases, and all the accessories of the tabernacle—the heaviest equipment that required wagons.
Describes the specific tasks of the sons of Merari in carrying the tabernacle's planks, pillars, and bases, explaining why they needed the most wagons and oxen.
The preceding verse shows that the sons of Gershon received two wagons and four oxen, fewer than the sons of Merari because their load was lighter.
The service of the sons of Gershon was to be carried out under the leadership of Ithamar, son of Aaron, in the same way as the sons of Merari.
Confirms that the service of the sons of Merari was under the supervision of Ithamar, the priest, son of Aaron.
Mentions Ithamar as one of Aaron's sons, who here has responsibility for leading the work of the Levites.
Ithamar had oversight of the Levites' work at the tabernacle, confirming his leadership role mentioned in this verse.
